ticket.title: Visit Notes workspace should accept a Encounter object for editing
ticket.text:
Visit Notes workspace should accept a Encounter object for editing

The Visit notes workspace is implemented to accept an `Encounter` object on edit mode. However, it actually uses the object as if it’s of type `MappedEncounter`, like `encounter.id`, `encounter.rawDatetime`. Typescript didn’t catch this because the `Encounter` type defined in esm-core allows arbitrary fields as `any` type. The workspace is also invoked by passing in a `MappedEncounter` object instead of an `Encounter` object, so this does not technically cause any user-facing issues. However, we should still fix this, as we recently made the visit notes workspace “exported” to be used in the service queues app, thus we are leaking a non-standard abstraction type to other apps.

understanding.intent: Update the Visit Notes workspace to accept a standard Encounter object instead of a MappedEncounter object when editing notes.

criteria.text: The Visit Notes workspace accepts an Encounter object when invoked in edit mode without causing user-facing regressions.
criteria.quote: Visit Notes workspace should accept a Encounter object for editing

questions: Are there specific editing workflows or apps (such as service queues) that should be regression tested in the browser after this prop change?

risks.detail: This is an internal code and TypeScript interface refactor for component props with no user-facing changes or visible browser behavior to test.

understanding.domain_reason: Editing visit notes and encounter data is a core clinical feature of OpenMRS 3.
understanding.reason: backend-only change: nothing a user can check in the browser, so UAT test cases do not apply
